title: Rabbi Abba bar Ada
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 4:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Gittin.4.6.3) relates that his maidservant fled to Kilisiya. He consulted Rabbi Mani, who ruled like Rabbi Immi. That is, he lived in the Land of Israel and she fled abroad; he asked whether he could sell her. Hyman identifies this as the later Rabbi Mana. He therefore distinguishes the subject from Rabbi Abba bar Rav Ada, who speaks in Rabbi Yitzchak’s name in [Shabbat 130a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.130a.18), where [Rav Yosef challenges the teaching](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.130b.1-2). In particular, Dikdukei Soferim reads Ravin bar Ada there; see that entry.[^1]

notes.text: The linked Yerushalmi has Rabbi Mana rule as Rabbi Immi did, distinguishing a sale from a loan for use. Guggenheimer renders Kilisiya as Cilicia. The linked Bavli gives Rabbi Abba bar Rav Ada, and Rav Yosef objects on the next folio. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=45&lang=en) records the variant Ravin in the Bavli notice. The identification of Mana and the distinction between the two Abbas are Hyman’s.
